name: Safelight
source: A darkroom at work — the amber safelight, sepia and selenium toner, the fixer tray
rationale: Everything lit by one amber lamp; prints toning from sepia to selenium plum. Warmth from light, not from cream and terracotta.
trend: The warm darks of 2026 (Silhouette, Mocha Mousse) — as light, not paint

name: Mood for Love
source: Wong Kar-wai & Christopher Doyle — In the Mood for Love, 2046, Chungking Express
rationale: Tobacco-and-rouge shadows, a cheongsam crimson, lamp gold — and the button is jade, the colour of the corridor's tiles.
trend: Divine Damson's deep reds and Hidden Gem's jade, given a film's light

name: Aquarium
source: A public aquarium after closing — tank light through dark water, coral, anemones
rationale: Deep blue-green dark lit from inside by one cyan tank, with coral and anemone violet drifting through it.
trend: Transformative Teal (CotY 2026) as light in water rather than a swatch

name: Basalt
source: Volcanic basalt with a sulphur crust and hot-spring minerals — Iceland, Danakil
rationale: Blue-black stone; the button is the sulphur crystal, and magma and a hot-spring teal glow from the cracks.
trend: Luminous Blue's cool depth (CotY 2027) as stone, Energy Orange as heat

name: Risograph
source: Risograph duotones — fluorescent pink, teal and yellow soy inks, slightly off-register
rationale: Clean grey stock and three printer's inks that overprint; the button is the fluorescent pink everyone remembers from a zine.
trend: SS27's 'loud and quiet together' (Rosy Future, Waterfall, Anise) as ink

name: Urushi
source: Japanese lacquerware — sumi ink, cinnabar, gold leaf and raden (abalone inlay)
rationale: Ink-black and lacquer; the button is aogai, the blue-violet flash of abalone shell, set against cinnabar and gold.
trend: Cloud Dancer's quiet (Pantone 2026) as ink; Lavender Oil grown into abalone
